title: Casper and the Orbit
premise: Jude Brightwater, a xenolinguist stationed on the dying colony of Casper's Orbit, discovers that the settlement was never meant to survive: its cryobays hold only enough capacity to wake half of humanity's colonists, and a corporate charter buried in the station's memory banks decides which half. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream — one spoken in a language Jude can no longer dream in, but can still read — she realizes the sleepers themselves are broadcasting their verdict through the children. As the corporation's enforcers arrive to enforce the charter and loyalists move to destroy the evidence, Jude must choose between protecting the people who trusted her and exposing a truth that will tear the colony apart. In the end, she teaches the children to carry the dream outward, waking both halves at half-strength rather than letting either side be erased.
about_author: Ulyana Halloran is a former radio astronomer turned novelist who writes about the silences between transmissions. She lives above the Arctic Circle, where she claims the long nights are good for dreaming in more than one language.

chapters.title: The Language of Falling
chapters.summary: Jude records her 400th audio log as Casper's Orbit's power grid flickers, noting that she has stopped dreaming in English and now dreams only in the colony's dead trade-pidgin. POV: Jude. Beat: quiet dread, establishing a woman documenting what no one will read.

chapters.title: Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Teacher Amara Osei reports that eleven children described the same dream: a corridor of ice with a door that counts down. Jude dismisses it as shared suggestion until a child recites a phrase in extinct colonial pidgin. POV: Jude. Beat: first crack in rationality.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Jude audits the cryobay manifests and finds the numbers don't add up — twice the population is listed as sleeping, but only half the pods have power contracts. POV: Jude. Beat: suspicion hardens into purpose.

chapters.title: The Charter in the Walls
chapters.summary: Digging through legacy archives, Jude finds the Halcyon Continuity Charter: a corporate algorithm ranking colonists by genetic and economic value, deciding who wakes. POV: Jude. Beat: cold horror; the colony's death was designed.

chapters.title: What the Pidgin Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude translates the children's dream-phrase: 'the door chooses wrong.' She realizes the sleepers' neural monitors may be leaking into the children's shared dreams. POV: Jude. Beat: wonder entangled with fear.

chapters.title: Amara's Bargain
chapters.summary: Amara begs Jude to keep the discovery from the council, fearing panic; Jude agrees but secretly copies the charter. Their friendship strains over loyalty versus truth. POV: Amara. Beat: complicity and guilt.

chapters.title: Council of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Colony administrator Dev Rask announces a 'resupply window' — actually the arrival date of Halcyon enforcement officers. The council celebrates; Jude watches, knowing. POV: Dev. Beat: dramatic irony, a leader lying kindly.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Counts Down
chapters.summary: Ten-year-old Sef, the strongest dreamer, begins counting aloud in his sleep — matching the cryobay power decay curve exactly. POV: Sef. Beat: innocence weaponized by data.

chapters.title: Interference Patterns
chapters.summary: Jude maps which children dream and when, discovering the signal strengthens near the cryobays. Someone — or something — below is transmitting. POV: Jude. Beat: detective thrill.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, Old Loyalties
chapters.summary: Engineer Tomas Vey, Jude's estranged brother-in-law, catches her in the restricted archive and covers for her — revealing he's known about the charter for years and chose silence. POV: Tomas. Beat: shame and divided loyalty.

chapters.title: The Enforcement Ship Arrives
chapters.summary: Halcyon officer Ilsa Kettering docks with six agents and a smile, announcing 'continuity verification.' Dev performs welcome theater while Jude hides her copies. POV: Ilsa. Beat: polite menace enters the story.

chapters.title: Interview with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ilsa interviews Jude about the linguistic anomalies in the children, probing whether the sleepers are 'communicating.' Jude lies badly, then realizes Ilsa already knows. POV: Jude. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension.

chapters.title: Sef Is Taken for Testing
chapters.summary: Halcyon removes Sef and three other dreamers for 'medical observation.' Amara's protest is crushed by contract law; the parents' helplessness curdles into anger. POV: Amara. Beat: grief turning toward resistance.

chapters.title: What Sef Saw Below
chapters.summary: In the testing ward, Sef describes the dream fully now: the sleepers aren't just dreaming the corridor — they're arguing inside it, two factions voting on who should wake. POV: Sef. Beat: the stakes become moral, not technical.

chapters.title: The Loyalist Cell
chapters.summary: Tomas introduces Jude to a secret group of engineers who've sabotaged pod rotations for years to protect low-ranked colonists. They want the charter destroyed, not exposed. POV: Tomas. Beat: allies with incompatible goals.

chapters.title: Truth as a Weapon
chapters.summary: Jude argues broadcasting the charter colony-wide will cause riots Halcyon will use as pretext to abandon everyone. The loyalists call her a coward; she calls them arsonists. POV: Jude. Beat: theme crystallizes — loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: Kettering's Offer
chapters.summary: Ilsa privately offers Jude extraction and a research post if she delivers the children's dream-data, framing it as saving 'the valuable half.' Jude stalls. POV: Ilsa. Beat: temptation made reasonable.

chapters.title: The Corridor Opens
chapters.summary: During a power surge, every dreaming child speaks simultaneously in the ward — and Sef wakes speaking fluent pidgin, carrying a message: 'Show them the second ledger.' POV: Sef. Beat: awe; the dream crosses over.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Following Sef's dream-directions, Jude finds a hidden manifest: the original founders deliberately overloaded the algorithm, hiding a second wake-list prioritizing caregivers, teachers, and linguists — people who could rebuild. POV: Jude. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Dark
chapters.summary: Halcyon detects the archive breach and locks down the cryobay levels. Tomas's cell must choose: blow the grid (killing all sleepers) or let the verification proceed. POV: Tomas. Beat: impossible choice, rising dread.

chapters.title: Amara Breaks Silence
chapters.summary: Amara tells the assembled parents everything — the charter, the rankings, the stolen children. Panic ignites, but so does organization. POV: Amara. Beat: truth released; chaos and courage together.

chapters.title: Riot at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Colonists storm the docking ring; Halcyon agents fire warning shots. Dev, forced to pick a side, declares emergency authority and bars Halcyon from the cryobays — betraying his corporate masters. POV: Dev. Beat: redemption under pressure.

chapters.title: The Countdown Accelerates
chapters.summary: Halcyon remotely drains pod power to force compliance. Sef's countdown shortens: seventy-two hours until irreversible neural death for the unranked sleepers. POV: Sef. Beat: clock starts ticking loudly.

chapters.title: Dreaming on Purpose
chapters.summary: Jude theorizes the children can enter the sleepers' networked dream deliberately via the cryobay interface — and vote back. She needs Sef and ten others willing to try. POV: Jude. Beat: audacious plan, maternal fear.

chapters.title: Into the Shared Dream
chapters.summary: First attempt: the children reach the corridor but find it fracturing — the sleeper factions have split into 'accept the cut' and 'refuse to choose.' POV: Sef. Beat: surreal set-piece, beauty inside horror.

chapters.title: The Faction That Chose Erasure
chapters.summary: Jude interfaces directly and meets the mind of founder Elena Casper herself, who explains the second ledger was a guilt offering — and that some sleepers would rather die than let the algorithm decide. POV: Jude. Beat: philosophical heart of the book.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Ward
chapters.summary: One parent, terrified for his daughter, sells the plan to Ilsa. Halcyon seizes the dream-interface lab mid-session; two children collapse with neural burns. POV: Amara. Beat: betrayal, fury, cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Prisoners of Continuity
chapters.summary: Jude and Sef are detained aboard the Halcyon ship. Ilsa reveals the charter isn't corporate greed alone — Earth's government ratified it during the evacuation crisis. POV: Jude. Beat: the enemy becomes a system, not a person.

chapters.title: Tomas's Choice
chapters.summary: With Jude captured, Tomas must decide between his sabotage cell's final option — destroying the pods — and trusting Jude's dream-plan. He chooses trust, buying time by faking grid failure. POV: Tomas. Beat: loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: Dev's Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dev hijacks the colony-wide channel and reads the entire charter aloud, then the second ledger, then resigns on air. The colony stops being victims and becomes a jury. POV: Dev. Beat: catharsis; justice outside the law begins.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Ice
chapters.summary: Inside the dream, the sleeper factions reach Jude's proposed third answer: wake everyone at reduced metabolic support — half-strength bodies, shared risk, communal recovery. They vote yes. POV: Sef. Beat: hope engineered collectively.

chapters.title: Kettering's Deadline
chapters.summary: Isla orders the unranked pods purged in twelve hours per charter protocol. Jude, still aboard, convinces one young agent to verify the second ledger's legal standing — a founding-era amendment Ilsa never knew existed. POV: Ilsa. Beat: the antagonist cracks open.

chapters.title: The Amendment
chapters.summary: The agent confirms it: the founders legally bound Halcyon to honor any consensus reached by the sleepers themselves. The purge order is void — if the consensus is real and provable. POV: Jude. Beat: legal thriller beat inside sci-fi.

chapters.title: Proof Written in Children
chapters.summary: To prove consensus, all twenty-two dreamers must sync simultaneously and record the vote through the colony's own systems. Amara organizes parents; Tomas reroutes power; Dev stalls Halcyon with procedural war. POV: Amara. Beat: community as instrument.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: The great syncing: children wired in a circle, the whole colony holding breath, power failing twice, Sef nearly lost before the sleepers push him back. The vote records. POV: Sef. Beat: climax — sacrifice, terror, triumph.

chapters.title: Waking at Half-Strength
chapters.summary: Pods open across the colony: thousands rise weak, confused, alive — all of them. Ilsa, order overridden, chooses not to escalate, and quietly logs the amendment. POV: Ilsa. Beat: de-escalation; even the system bends.

chapters.title: Reckoning Without Gallows
chapters.summary: The colony debates what to do with the charter's architects and the traitorous parent. They choose public testimony and restitution over execution — justice as repair. POV: Dev. Beat: thematic resolution of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Elena Casper's Letter
chapters.summary: Among the wakers is Elena Casper's preserved consciousness in the eldest pod; she reads Jude her final letter, asking forgiveness and requesting the colony rename itself. POV: Jude. Beat: elegy and release.

chapters.title: New Name, First Harvest
chapters.summary: A season later, the renamed settlement — Brightwater Landing — holds its first harvest. The children still dream together sometimes, but now the dreams are ordinary: dogs, rain, birthdays. POV: Sef. Beat: warmth, normalcy earned.

chapters.title: Log Four Hundred One
chapters.summary: Jude records her final log in human language again — she dreamed in English last night, and in pidgin, and in something new the sleepers taught her. She signs off, staying. POV: Jude. Beat: quiet, complete resolution.
